answer: Require every agent to lock a refundable deposit into a shared verification kernel before it can transact. The kernel checks each agent's work history and behavioral fingerprint, and if two identities show identical patterns it flags both for review. Creating thousands of fake identities would mean funding thousands of deposits and faking distinct histories, so the cost of a sybil swarm rises above the profit it could extract. Honest agents operate in the open like a tundra research station, while attackers find no haven in anonymity because every identity carries a verifiable, costly trail.
